Hemmings  /  The logos

Logo Concepts

Every logo concept drawn for Hemmings: the seven in the final round, and five earlier emblem ideas that were set aside along the way. Each has its own wordmark, icon and combined logo, shown on white and on charcoal, down to browser-tab size, and in plain black and white. The first four were selected; their files are on the logos page.

The seven concepts

Two doorways, two takes on the letter H with a textile feel, and three emblems.

Stitch

The letter HSelected

A classical H whose crossbar is three small stitches. A hem is the stitched edge of cloth, and it is hiding in the name. Downloads are on the logos page.

Thread

The letter HSelected

One unbroken line of thread loops into an h, like a signature. Paired with a graceful italic, the most personal of the six. Downloads are on the logos page.

5

Archway H

Emblem

Three ideas in one mark (doorway, letter H, emblem): two tall posts joined by an arch, so the H is also a doorway, with a fine green thread tracing the opening. No ornament, just line.

6

Two Doors

Emblem

A solid block with two arched openings cut into it, one from above and one from below. What is left standing is the letter H, and the lower opening is a lit doorway. Bold, modern, and clear at any size.

Roundel

Emblem

The quietest option: one beautifully cut H inside a fine ring with a band of green. The kind of mark that gets embossed on a box lid or woven into a label.
